summary: The original Engine.dll start-up path was driven end to end in a host process: window, settings, Engine construction, host-side publish, and Engine::Initialize, which returned normally and left both the GraphicsEngine and the Options objects in place.

observations.exports_resolved: windctor 0x7ffb63b07710, wininit 0x7ffb63b079b0, settings 0x7ffb639806e0, engine 0x7ffb63962930, engineinit 0x7ffb639643d0, filesystem 0x7ffb63976370
observations.window: WinWindow::Initialize returned 1 and IsWindow was true
observations.settings: default ctor produced the direct3d11 string with length 10; an explicit +0x0c of 2 was accepted
observations.engine: Engine::Engine produced vtable 0x7ffb63c2e2f0 which equals base+0x33E2F0, exactly the expected value

first_attempt_failure.fix: construct a real FileSystem with FileSystem::FileSystem() 0x86370 and pass it

symbol_learned: The four trailing std::string parameters belong to LocalizationManager::InitializeLanguage(string const&, string const&, string const&, string const&) and are localisation names; the two I supplied were "english".
benign_noise: 0x40010006 is STATUS_MS_VC_EXCEPTION and 0xE06D7363 is a C++ throw caught by the engine; neither is a failure.
boundary: The publish of the Engine pointer into Engine.dll+0x421428 was performed by this host. It reproduces the game operation but is not a recovery of the game's own publish code.
